sentences.text: Pangilinan remains chairman and chief executive, and in October 2026 he completed a 2.19-billion-peso purchase of additional Meralco shares from San Miguel Global Power Holdings.

At the annual stockholders' meeting on June 30, 2026, the board was refreshed with retail entrepreneur Bernido H. Liu and banker Bernadine T. Siy as independent directors, replacing Artemio V. Panganiban, lead independent director since 2008, and Pedro Emilio O. Roxas, after both reached regulatory term limits.

sentences.quote: "There is an approved one for 2026, of course. But I doubt whether we will reduce it for Meralco and MGEN (Meralco PowerGen Corp.)," Meralco Chairman Manuel V. Pangilinan told reporters on Tuesday.
sentences.text: In March 2026 Pangilinan said the 2026 capital expenditure program for Meralco and Meralco PowerGen was unlikely to be cut despite a group-wide budget review, framing the task as growing responsibly with financial discipline.

sentences.text: Under chairman and CEO Manuel Velez Pangilinan, Meralco's 2025 consolidated core net income rose 12 percent to 50.57 billion pesos as generation sales jumped 78 percent while distribution sales slipped 1 percent.
Capital spending surged 144 percent to 108.96 billion pesos for power plants and networks, funded largely by a 143 percent rise in borrowings to about 230 billion pesos.
A board-approved dividend policy provides for regular cash dividends equal to 50 percent of audited consolidated core earnings, though the 2024 payout reached 60 percent of core EPS.

sentences.text: Meralco's regulated Manila-area distribution franchise remains the earnings base, with net system input steady at 28,165 GWh in the first half of 2026 and an all-time high peak demand of 9.39 GW recorded on 28 May 2026.

Generation is the growth engine: Meralco PowerGen's core net income contribution rose 11 percent to 10.5 billion pesos, or 39 percent of group total, helped by the full six-month contribution of domestic LNG assets and new solar operations.

The 200-billion-peso MTerra Solar project, whose Phase 1 was inaugurated in July 2026 with 600 MW ready for commercial delivery and 250 MW under Phase 2 targeted for 2027, lets the group pass its 1,500 MW renewables goal three years early.
